subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs, model & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps - technical deep dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Hi John / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we're aligned.

Summary of the customer goals / pain points
- Primary goal: embed real-time summarization and in-chat suggestions into Acme's support UI with strict latency goals.
- Current pain: on-prem legacy infra yields high variability; peaks cause p95 latency spikes to >1.2s.
- Cost sensitivity: predictable per-transaction unit economics to budget for 100k daily active users.

Technical requirements you called out
- Target p50 latency: <= 120 ms for 256-token prompts (interactive hints).
- Target p95 latency: <= 350 ms (hard SLO for user-facing flows).
- Throughput: sustained 300 requests/sec for peak region (US-East), bursting to 600 rps for short windows.
- Model family: initially a 13B encoder-decoder / chat model with lower-cost 70B only for high-fidelity batch rerank jobs.
- Model behavior: must preserve strict safety filtering and deterministic reranking for internal workflows.
- Data security: logs retention window 30 days; SOC 2 evidence required; on-prem or VPC deployment preferred.

Deployment topology we discussed
- Preferred: Redwood Private (VPC) in AWS us-east-1, customer-managed VPC peering, KMS for key management.
- Fallback: Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity for failover (different region for DR).
- Autoscaling: horizontal worker pools + autoscaler tuned for constant tail latency; we recommended maintaining 2x baseline capacity for warm KV cache.

Attachments
- attached: acme-deep-dive-slide-deck.pdf (slides from today), acme-slo-requirements.xlsx (template with numbers you provided).

Proposed next steps
1) From Acme: confirm which flows are user-facing vs batch and provide sample QPS by flow (due Fri 3/13).
2) From Redwood: schedule architecture session with infra engs (Aditya + Dev) to map deployment topology and run a quick perf estimate (propose Mon 3/15).
3) Agreement: we'll produce an initial sizing + cost estimate and a minimal canary run plan.

If that aligns, I'll send a calendar invite for Mon and loop in Aditya and Dev.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

From: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps - technical deep dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Thanks Marissa - this looks great and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 120 ms p50 and 350 ms p95 numbers are for the UI hint generation flow (256-token prompts). For the longer context summarization flow (up to 1k tokens) p95 can be relaxed to 900 ms.
- QPS breakdown (rough): UI hints 250 rps sustained (peaks 500), summarization batch ~30 rps, rerank jobs 20 rps (batch).
- Model: we'd like to evaluate the 13B quantized variant first for cost reasons. For reranking, we can route to a higher-capacity 34B model if latency constraints allow (batch only).
- Security: SOC 2 is mandatory; we'll need the SOC 2 report + data flow diagram.

Next steps - confirmed
- We'll send the flow-level QPS spreadsheet by EOD Fri 3/13.
- Monday session works for us; Priya and I can join at 10am PT.

Appreciate the quick turnaround - excited to see the sizing.

Best,
John
Director, Customer AI Platform | Acme Corporation
john.smith@acme.com | +1 415-222-3344

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: ACME deep-dive follow-up - perf targets & ask for initial sizing

Aditya / Dev,

Looping you in on ACME's perf targets and topology ask. Key points from client:
- p50 <= 120 ms (256 tokens), p95 <= 350 ms (256 tokens). Longer summarization flow p95 <= 900 ms (1k tokens).
- Sustained 300 rps (US), burst to 600 rps.
- Prefer Redwood Private (VPC) in us-east-1 with KMS and 30d retention. SOC 2 evidence required.
- Model candidate: quantized 13B for interactive, 34B/70B for batch/rerank as needed.

Can you both:
1) Provide an initial instance sizing + GPU type recommendation (and estimated reserved capacity) for the interactive pool to meet p95 target with 256-token prompts. Assume 2x baseline warm capacity and explain assumptions on KV cache hit rate.
2) Call out tradeoffs if we quantize (FP16 vs 4-bit) and expected latency impact.
3) List any immediate red flags for a VPC/private deployment (network egress, peering requirements, KMS policies).

Client prefers Mon 3/15 10:00am PT for architecture review - I'll send the invite once I have your availability. Thanks!

-Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME deep-dive follow-up - perf targets & ask for initial sizing

Thanks Marissa - I can take the sizing draft. Initial notes:
- Recommend A100 80GB or equivalent for interactive 13B quantized (4-bit) to hit p95 targets with 2x warm workers; will run microbenchmarks Mon and share numbers.
- KV cache: expect 60-75% effective prefix cache hit for UI flows; 2x warm keeps tail stable.
- Quantization: 4-bit int can reduce memory and improve throughput but may add ~10-25% latency variance depending on kernel availability; FP16 safer with slightly higher cost.
- No immediate VPC blockers; will validate KMS policy and propose a peering checklist before Mon.

I'll post a short sizing doc + cost estimate by EOD Mon 3/15.

- Dev
Staff Backend Engineer | Redwood Inference
